task.goal: Fix the lost update on `PATCH /api/tasks/:id` and add task versions. (1) `src/db.ts`: append a NEW migration `ALTER TABLE tasks ADD COLUMN version INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1` (never edit a shipped one). (2) `src/tasks.ts`: add `version: number` to `Task` and `TaskView` and to `toView`, so every task the API answers carries it; `createTask` yields 1. (3) `updateTask`: today it reads the task, runs `readInput`, awaits `activity.record`, then UPDATEs every column from the stale snapshot — that is the bug. Rework it so the read, the version check and the write happen in one synchronous `transaction` with no await in between: re-read the task inside the transaction, UPDATE only the columns present in the body (so a PATCH without `version` never overwrites a field changed at the same time, AC4), set `version = version + 1` and `updated_at`, and when the body has a `version` (must be a positive integer, else 400) compare it to the current one and, on mismatch, change nothing and answer 409 with exactly `{"error": "version conflict", "task": <current TaskView>}` (add a `conflict`-style error in `src/http.ts` that carries the extra `task` field and make `send`/the router in `src/app.ts` return it). A PATCH that changes nothing must not bump the version. Compute `changes` against the fresh row, record the activity entry after the commit, and keep the reminder rescheduling (`jobs.scheduleReminder`) on due_date/assignee_id/done with the fresh row. Keep the owner check (`loadTask`/`loadList`). (4) Tests in `test/tasks.test.ts` (use `test/helpers.ts`): first a test that reproduces the race — two PATCHes fired concurrently without awaiting each (e.g. rename + done via `Promise.all`) and both changes must be present afterwards; it fails on the current code and passes after the fix; plus version=1 on create and on a pre-existing task (migrate a database at the old schema), version +1 per change and not on a no-op, 409 with the current task and nothing changed, PATCH with the right version succeeds. (5) `public/tasks.js` (+ `public/api.js` if needed): the page remembers each task's `version` as read and sends it in `patch(task, changes)`; on a 409 it shows the task as it is now (the `task` from the response, e.g. refresh the list and show a message like "This task changed elsewhere; showing its current state" in the error box) instead of a bare error; `api()` must expose the 409 body (e.g. attach `data` to the thrown Error). (6) `README.md`: document `version` in the task object (around line 54) and the optional `version` on `PATCH /api/tasks/:id` with the `409` answer and body (around line 63). Run the project's checks (`package.json` scripts) before finishing.

criteria.why: The read, version check and write now run in one synchronous transaction with no await. Only changed columns are written, so concurrent edits to different fields no longer overwrite each other.
The migration adds `version INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1`. `version = version + 1` runs only on real changes, and `toView` exposes it on every task answer.
A stale `version` throws a 409 with `{error, task}` from inside the transaction, so nothing is written. `fail` returns the custom body, and invalid versions get a 400.
Without `version` the PATCH skips the check and updates only the changed columns, re-read inside the transaction. The test fires 5 parallel PATCHes.
The parallel-PATCH test would have failed against the old await-between-read-and-write code. The version-count test adds a second check.
The page sends `version` and re-renders on a 409, and the README documents both. The conflict handling is untested. The message shows only the title, not what changed.

findings.what: `activity.record` now runs after the transaction commits. If it fails, the task is changed and versioned but the client gets a 500, and there is no activity entry. Before, the log was written first. The log and the change are no longer atomic, and the order of log entries under concurrency is no longer tied to the order of writes.

The UPDATE builds its SQL from `changes` keys. This is safe only because `readInput` whitelists the keys, and nothing in this code enforces that. A comment or an explicit column whitelist would be safer.

The pre-version migration test hard-codes `PRAGMA user_version = 6` and drops the column, so it is brittle when migrations are added. There is no test for a concurrent PATCH that carries a version, for a conflict on a tags-only PATCH, or for the front-end conflict path.

After a 409 the page re-renders and shows only a message with the title. The user's rejected change is dropped without being shown, and the user is not offered a retry. This is acceptable but minimal. `err.data.task` is used without a guard.
A stale `version` on a PATCH that would change nothing still returns 409. This is defensible. The ticket does not cover it, and the README does not mention it.

judge.summary: The diff fixes the lost-update race. It makes the read, check and write one synchronous transaction, writes only changed columns, and adds version tracking with a 409 path, README text and front-end handling. Moving the activity log write after the commit is a non-atomic regression, and the front-end conflict path and some concurrency cases are untested.
